When I write a long chunk of Arabizi lines, I lose variety and repeat the same patterns ("azdak mn emta la emta",
"li fetou", "zoret", "nisan"). Christina (2026-11-19): "its either correct OR varied with you, never both".

**Why:** the model has to generalise to real users, who vary spelling, wording and laziness ("Zaatar w Zeit" alone
instead of "la2, azde Zaatar w Zeit"); repeated phrases teach it one pattern and make it break on others.

**How to apply:** before writing a chunk, build a variation table per concept from her approved forms (grammar notes)
and rotate through it on purpose, counting uses; never use a phrase she has not approved or seen as if it were common
("li fet"); keep formal words rare ("zoret"); vary months, periods and sentence shapes; include lazy short answers.
Check the chunk's phrase counts before showing it.
- (2026-11-20) Vary EVERY common word, not only the one the set is about: in 21 abel mbereh lines I rotated the period
  but used "adde" 9 times and "wen" for every where. Her: "stop varying one word forgetting the rest". How much:
  adde / aday / adey / adeysh / addesh / 2adesh; where: wen / wain / wayn; day before: abel / abl / 2abel / awalt.
- (2026-11-20) I also over-double letters (2alle, sajjalto): people type 2ale, sajalto. Single letters by default. Related: [[lebanese-arabizi-grammar-notes]],
[[review-silence-means-approved]].
- (2026-11-22) Double letters in stored data (3eddele, el marraat, ...): lessen their count where they are the
  overwhelming majority, so single letters lead (her ruling; part 6). Not wrong, just less common.
